candidate.title: Aba-Seq
candidate.scope: The assigned Illumina bulk Aba-seq schematic, from hydroxymethylated genomic DNA through glucosylation, AbaSI cleavage, biotinylated-adapter ligation, fragmentation and streptavidin selection to the terminal DNA product. Aba-Seq and Aba-seq name the same target here. The left-hand hydroxymethylome motif is explanatory, not a second branch. scAba-seq, the PvuRts1I adaptation and SCL-exo are discussed or cited by the catalogue but are not depicted alternatives and do not expand this extraction. The primary bulk implementation clarifies adapter identity and the cleavage-end readout; its unshown downstream library completion is not decomposed into diagram operations.

operations.label: T4-βGT
operations.description: Glucosylate 5hmC in the starting genomic DNA, producing DNA with glucosylated 5hmC.
operations.information_effect: Creates the modification recognized preferentially by AbaSI while retaining genomic sequence association.

operations.label: AbaSI
operations.description: Cleave glucosylated genomic DNA to produce double-stranded fragments with staggered ends near the recognized modified sites.
operations.mechanism: AbaSI recognizes 5gmC and cleaves at a narrow range of distances from it. It prefers symmetrically positioned cytosines around the cut, one glucosylated and the other modified or unmodified; the primary paper reports lower cleavage efficiency when only one 5gmC is present.
operations.information_effect: Converts proximity to glucosylated 5hmC into a DNA-end coordinate that can later be mapped. Sequence and modification context affect which target sites are represented efficiently.

evidence.quote: One member in the family, AbaSI, recognizes 5-glucosylatedmethylcytosine (5gmC) with high specificity when compared to 5mC and C, and cleaves at a narrow range of distances away from the recognized modified cytosine.

AbaSI prefers sites with two cytosines positioned symmetrically around the cleavage site: one is 5gmC and the other can be modified or not (Figure 1A). AbaSI cleaves with a lower efficiency when only one 5gmC is present (Wang et al., 2011).

operations.label: Ligate
operations.description: Ligate the depicted biotinylated oligonucleotides onto AbaSI-cleaved DNA ends, producing adapter-tagged fragments.
operations.mechanism: The primary paper identifies the added oligonucleotides as biotinylated P1b adapters with randomized two-base 3′ overhangs.
operations.information_effect: Attaches the biotin capture handle and preserves the AbaSI-end association used for sequencing from P1b.

method_scopes.rationale: All five depicted transformations belong to the single Aba-seq route. T4-βGT and AbaSI are catalysts, the biotinylated oligonucleotide is an added ligation substrate, and streptavidin beads are the capture support. No compartment, barcode, pooling or parallel target workflow is drawn. The primary Aba-seq paper supports this sequence and explains that 5hmC is inferred from nearby mapped cleavage sites, rather than read directly as a distinct base. Cleavage efficiency is site-dependent and exact-base assignment can be ambiguous; the primary data report about 13% ambiguous cleavage sites, not universal perfect single-base resolution.

evidence.quote: Single-cell 5hmC sequencing reveals chromosome-wide cell-to-cell variability and enables lineage reconstruction.

The epigenetic DNA modification 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) has crucial roles in development and gene regulation. Quantifying the abundance of this epigenetic mark at the single-cell level could enable us to understand its roles. We present a single-cell, genome-wide and strand-specific 5hmC sequencing technology, based on 5hmC glucosylation and glucosylation-dependent digestion of DNA, that reveals pronounced cell-to-cell variability in the abundance of 5hmC on the two DNA strands of a given chromosome. We develop a mathematical model that reproduces the strand bias and use this model to make two predictions. First, the variation in strand bias should decrease when 5hmC turnover increase
evidence.rationale: Only the supplied abstract was inspected for method content. This single-cell variation is mentioned in the catalogue but is not a target of the assigned bulk Aba-seq schematic; its complete library architecture is not established by this abstract.

evidence.quote: A sensitive approach to map genome-wide 5-hydroxymethylcytosine and 5-formylcytosine at single-base resolution.

Mapping genome-wide 5-hydroxymethylcytosine (5hmC) and 5-formylcytosine (5fC) at single-base resolution is important to understand their biological functions. We present a cost-efficient mapping method that combines 5hmC-specific restriction enzyme PvuRts1I with a 5hmC chemical labeling enrichment method. The sensitive method enables detection of low-abundance 5hmC sites, providing a more complete 5hmC landscape than available bisulfite-based methods. This method generated a genome-wide 5fC map at single-base resolution. evidence.quote: Advances in the profiling of DNA modifications: cytosine methylation and beyond.
